## Overview

Two middleware functions extend Analytics.js (snippet version 4.12.0+) with custom client-side event handling:
- **Source middleware** — manipulate/filter payloads before Segment receives them
- **Destination middleware** — manipulate/filter payloads per destination (device-mode only)

Both run in the browser with full DOM and Browser API access.

## Source Middleware

```js
analytics.addSourceMiddleware(({ payload, next, integrations }) => {
  // mutate payload.obj to transform the event
  next(payload)  // required to proceed; omit/return null to drop
})
```

**Parameters:**
- `payload.obj` — event payload; mutate this to transform
- `next(payload)` — call to pass event to next middleware or Segment. Omit or return `null` to drop the event
- `integrations` — array of integration objects; set to falsy to block specific destinations

**Example: modify track event**
```js
analytics.addSourceMiddleware(({ payload, next }) => {
    const { event } = payload.obj.context
    if (event.type === 'track') {
      event.event.toLowerCase()
    }
    next(payload)
});
```

**Example: drop invalid events**
```js
analytics.addSourceMiddleware(({ payload, next }) => {
  const { event } = payload.obj.context
  if (!isValid(event)) {
    return null // event is dropped
  }
  next(payload)
});
```

## Destination Middleware

```js
analytics.addDestinationMiddleware('integrationName', ({ payload, next, integration }) => {
  // mutate payload.obj to transform
  next(payload)  // required to proceed; omit/return null to drop
})
```

**Parameters:**
- `payload.obj` — event payload; mutate to transform
- `next(payload)` — call to proceed. Omit or return `null` to drop for this destination only
- `integration` — string name of target integration; use `'*'` to target all destinations (excluding Segment.io)

**Note:** Destination middleware only affects device-mode destinations. Server-side (cloud-mode) destination transforms must happen server-side.

**Example: modify event before sending to integrationA**
```js
analytics.addDestinationMiddleware('integrationA', ({ payload, next, integration }) => {
  delete payload.obj.pageTitle;
  next(payload);
});
```

**Example: drop invalid events for specific destination**
```js
analytics.addDestinationMiddleware('integrationA', ({ payload, next, integration }) => {
  const { event } = payload.obj.context
  if (!isValid(event)) {
    return null // event is dropped
  }
  next(payload)
});
```

## Registration & Execution

- Call `.addSourceMiddleware()` and `.addDestinationMiddleware()` as many times as needed
- Register before or after `.load()`
- **Source middleware runs first**, in registration order, before any destination middleware
- Destination middleware runs per-destination, in registration order
- Omitting `next()` in any middleware drops the event (for that destination, if destination middleware)

## Braze Deduplication Middleware

Optional built-in middleware (disabled by default) reduces Braze costs by skipping Identify calls with duplicate traits:
- Sends only when ≥1 trait value changed
- Skips duplicate-trait Identify events
- Enable in Analytics.js source settings under "Braze Debounce Identify"
- Details: [segment-braze-mobile-middleware](https://github.com/segmentio/segment-braze-mobile-middleware)
